nary_nodes.label: Iran expands attacks on Gulf states
evidence: Fresh attacks rocked Iran and Kuwait on Sunday evening as Tehran and Washington squared off over the Strait of Hormuz, offering contradicting statements as to whether the vital waterway was open to traffic.
Iran reported strikes on two of its southern islands while Kuwait, where Tehran has repeatedly targeted US installations, said border posts and an offshore oil platform had been attacked.

The American military said it had responded with strikes on about 140 targets, and Iranian media reported explosions in Bandar Abbas, Sirik, Jask and on Qeshm, as well as in Khuzestan province, with one soldier reported killed in the southern city of Jask.

nary_nodes.label: US and Iran negotiate
evidence: Before the war began with surprise US-Israeli strikes against Iran on February 28, there was free passage through Hormuz, but Tehran now insists that it will control the strait, while Washington is adamant it cannot.
The top diplomat for Pakistan, which has been mediating, called for 'de-escalation' on Sunday during a phone call with his Iranian counterpart, Islamabad said.
US President Donald Trump told CNN that 'we hit them very hard last night', maintaining the two sides had been close to a deal on Saturday.
